=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- agents.md | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The PR appends this text straight into `agents.md`. Section 25 of the unattended instructions says never to add text to `agents.md` directly, even when an issue asks to "document this in agents.md". The required route is a fragment such as `agents.d/7053-<slug>.md`, starting with `<!-- agents: section="<exact ## heading>" -->`. The PR adds no fragment and no `agents.d/` file; the glob found none.
  WHY: Another open PR or integration branch that edits the same `agents.md` region will hit a merge conflict, and the conflict resolver or integration self-heal may give up, as in the cited incident.
- agents.md | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The note says the two hook copies already match on `main` and that the drift may exist only on PR #6830's head. Its removal condition is "byte-identical on the affected branch". If #6830 merges, closes or is rebased with no drift, nothing tells a maintainer to delete the paragraph.
  WHY: This is documentation drift only, with no runtime effect. The paragraph can stay in `agents.md` as stale operator guidance.

=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- agents.md | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The PR directly modifies agents.md to add the operator-step paragraph.
  WHY: The unattended system instructions (§25) strictly prohibit direct edits to agents.md, as this is a known source of concurrent edit conflicts in long-running integration branches.
- agents.md | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The instructions for removing the note ("When the copies are byte-identical...") lack a clear, observable trigger or verification step for the automated systems to know when it is safe to remove.
  WHY: This creates permanent documentation drift, as the note may remain in agents.md indefinitely even after the manual operator step is completed and verified.
- Requirement: Add the unblock note to agents.md using the agents fragment system per §25 of the unattended system instructions.
  Expected change site: agents.d/7053-merge-guard-live-parity-operator-step.md
  Evidence of absence: The PR directly edited agents.md instead of creating an agents.d fragment for the new note.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- agents.md | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The PR adds a new operator-step paragraph directly to `agents.md` rather than writing an `agents.d/<issue>-<slug>.md` fragment. `unattended_system_instructions.md` §25 says "Never add text to `agents.md` (or `AGENTS.md` in a consumer repo) directly, even when a plan, issue, or review finding says 'document this in agents.md'."
  WHY: This is a documentation convention defect rather than a runtime failure. Today the rule is unenforced: the precedent `WRAPPED_GIT_WRITE_GUARD_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP` was added the same way and retired by direct edit (see the existing "former `WRAPPED_GIT_WRITE_GUARD_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP` placeholder is retired" paragraph at line 555 and `changelog.d/6755-merged-pr-guard-shell-wrappers.md`). The defect surfaces only once the fragment infrastructure lands.
- agents.md | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The note claims both copies were "byte-identical on `main` when this note was written, so the drift may exist only on that branch" (PR #6830's head), then sets the removal condition to "byte-identical on the affected branch". The affected branch is a temporary PR head that will be merged, closed, or rebased; once gone or once rebased onto `main`, the removal condition references a branch that no longer exists.
  WHY: Documentation drift — the note has no automated retirement signal and depends on a person editing agents.md in place after the operator step completes.
- Requirement: "Keep the new behaviour off until a person finishes the operator step: gate it behind `MERGE_GUARD_LIVE_PARITY_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP` (a feature flag that defaults off, or a placeholder env var that makes the code skip safely)." (Linked issue, third paragraph)
  Expected change site: any code/script/test that would have to read the placeholder to gate behaviour — i.e. a real gate somewhere, or an explicit acknowledgement that no behaviour is gated today.
  Evidence of absence: `grep` for `MERGE_GUARD_LIVE_PARITY_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP` returns only the two new mentions in `agents.md` line 558 and the changelog fragment at line 2; no workflow, script, or test reads the placeholder. The new agents.md paragraph itself states "no workflow, script or test reads it, and setting it changes nothing".
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
